newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 18.95 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 18.95 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEM bills fell 204 basis points to 18.95 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 20 billion bolivars of 180- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 20.99 percent coupon for a price of 100.93 pct. At last week's auction, the six-month notes yielded 20.99 percent.

The bank also sold five billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 21.52 percent coupon at a price of 100.22 percent, and five billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 22.08 percent coupon at an average price of 99.74 percent.
Yields for these notes fell 283 basis points to 21.17 percent for the 269-day bills, and 236 basis points to 22.39 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
